points: Particles (を, で, に, へ)

title: Action particles
titleJp: どこで なにを しますか
canDo: I can say what I do, where I do it and where I go, with を, で and に / へ in the right place.
I can look at a sentence and name the job of each block (topic, time, place, destination, object, predicate) just from its particle.
I can choose between で and に by asking: does the person do something there, or go there?
I can contrast things with は: "Coffee, I drink; alcohol, I don't".
I can build a sentence from loose blocks: verb at the end, topic and time at the start.

skills: Conjugating the Lesson 3 verbs into 〜ます / 〜ません (lesson 03-1).
Knowing that は marks the topic and is read wa (lesson 01-1).
A dense lesson: do it in 2 sessions. Session 1 goes up to point 4c; session 2 starts at 4d and includes the homework.

vocab.en: what (the form used before を: なにを)
but, however (at the start of a sentence)

grammar.title: を: the object
grammar.explanation:
A sentence with a verb is a row of **blocks**, and each block is [word + particle]. The particle is the **label** that says what job that block does. The first label in this lesson is **を** (read **o**).
• を goes **after** the thing that receives the action: what is eaten, drunk, watched, read, listened to or done. The block [thing + を] is the **OBJECT**, and it answers the question **"what?"** asked of the verb at the end.
• コーヒーを のみます: "I drink what?" → coffee.
• The label goes **after** the word. English says "I drink coffee"; Japanese says "coffee-を drink".
• With する, the object is often an activity: テニスを します ("I play tennis", literally "I do tennis").
• Questions: replace the thing with **なに** and keep を: なにを たべますか。 ("What do you eat?")
• Verbs of movement (いく, くる, かえる) do **not** take を to say where someone goes: the destination has a different label (point 4c).

examples.jp: アナさんは ざっしを よみます。
examples.kana: アナさんは ざっしを よみます。

examples.jp: ルーカスさんは よる おんがくを ききます。
examples.kana: ルーカスさんは よる おんがくを ききます。
examples.romaji: Rūkasu-san wa yoru ongaku o kikimasu.
examples.en: Lucas listens to music at night.

examples.jp: なにを たべますか。— すしを たべます。
examples.kana: なにを たべますか。— すしを たべます。
examples.romaji: Nani o tabemasu ka. — Sushi o tabemasu.
examples.en: What will you eat? — I'll eat sushi.

pitfalls: を is read "o", but it is always written with を: コーヒーお ✗ → コーヒーを ✓.
A destination is not an object: だいがくを いきます ✗ → だいがくに いきます ✓.
"What" before を is なに: なんを のみますか ✗ → なにを のみますか ✓.
howToStudy: For each Lesson 3 verb, say out loud one thing + を: ほんを よみます, おちゃを のみます, テレビを みます…
Tap 🔬 on the examples: the block with を shows up as OBJECT. Ask the ★ PREDICATE "what?" and check that the answer is that block.
In your notebook, write 3 sentences "I do X" and 3 "I don't do X" (〜を 〜ません).

grammar.title: で: where the action happens
grammar.explanation:
で marks **the place where an action happens**: the stage where someone eats, studies, watches or plays. The block [place + で] is the **PLACE** of the action, and it answers **"where does it happen?"**.
• としょかんで べんきょうします: I study where? → at the library.
• Use で with **activity** verbs: たべる, のむ, みる, よむ, きく, する, べんきょうする…
• English helps here: "**at / in** the library" for where you do something is で; "**to** the library" for where you go is に / へ (next point). The question that decides it is: **does the person do something there (で) or go there (に)?**
• Questions: どこで 〜ますか。 ("Where do you…?")
• Saying where a thing **is** (exists) is a different structure, with に and another verb (lesson 04-1).
• で has one more use, the **means** ("by bus"), which waits until lesson 10-3. In this lesson, で = the place of the action.
grammar.structure: [place] で [object] を [verb]  → で answers "where does it happen?"

examples.jp: わたしは としょかんで ほんを よみます。
examples.kana: わたしは としょかんで ほんを よみます。
examples.romaji: Watashi wa toshokan de hon o yomimasu.
examples.en: I read books at the library.

examples.jp: すずきさんは だいがくで テニスを します。
examples.kana: すずきさんは だいがくで テニスを します。
examples.romaji: Suzuki-san wa daigaku de tenisu o shimasu.
examples.en: Mr./Ms. Suzuki plays tennis at the university.

examples.jp: どこで ひるごはんを たべますか。— がっこうで たべます。
examples.kana: どこで ひるごはんを たべますか。— がっこうで たべます。
examples.romaji: Doko de hirugohan o tabemasu ka. — Gakkō de tabemasu.
examples.en: Where do you eat lunch? — I eat at school.

pitfalls: A place of activity takes で: としょかんに べんきょうします ✗ → としょかんで べんきょうします ✓.
A place you go to does not take で: リオで いきます ✗ → リオに いきます ✓.

English uses "in / at" both for where you do something and for where something is. Japanese splits them: で is only for where an **action** happens; where something simply **is** uses に and another verb (lesson 04-1).
howToStudy: Think of 3 places in your routine (うち, だいがく, としょかん…) and say out loud what you do in each one: うちで 〜を 〜ます。
The question test: before choosing で or に, ask "do they DO something there, or GO there?". Do this out loud with every sentence in the homework.
Tap 🔬 on the examples: the block with で shows up as PLACE. Read the ★ PREDICATE and ask it "where?".

grammar.title: に / へ: where to (destination)
grammar.explanation:
に and へ mark the **destination** of verbs of movement: いく (to go), くる (to come), かえる (to go back home). The block [place + に / へ] is the **DESTINATION**, and it answers **"where to?"**.
• だいがくに いきます = だいがくへ いきます: "I go to the university".
• As a particle, へ is read **e**, not "he" — just as は is read wa.
• For destinations the two are practically interchangeable. へ puts a little more weight on the **direction** ("toward"); に, on the **point of arrival**. When in doubt, use に.
• に has other uses that へ doesn't, such as clock times (しちじに, lesson 03-3). So **へ is only for direction**.
• かえる means going back to your base: うちに かえります (I go home), ブラジルに かえります (I go back to Brazil).
• Questions: どこに いきますか。 / どこへ いきますか。
grammar.structure: [destination] に / へ [いく・くる・かえる]  → answers "where to?"

examples.jp: マリアさんは あした リオに いきます。
examples.kana: マリアさんは あした リオに いきます。
examples.romaji: Maria-san wa ashita Rio ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Maria is going to Rio tomorrow.

examples.jp: たなかさんは にほんへ かえります。
examples.kana: たなかさんは にほんへ かえります。
examples.en: Mr./Ms. Tanaka is going back to Japan.

examples.jp: どこへ いきますか。— としょかんに いきます。
examples.kana: どこへ いきますか。— としょかんに いきます。
examples.romaji: Doko e ikimasu ka. — Toshokan ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Where are you going? — I'm going to the library.

pitfalls: へ as a particle is read "e": にほんへ = "Nihon he" ✗ → "Nihon e" ✓.
English "go home" has no "to", but Japanese still needs the destination particle — and it is never を or で: うち かえります ✗ / うちを かえります ✗ / うちで かえります ✗ → うちに かえります ✓.
へ does not mark clock times: しちじへ おきます ✗ → しちじに おきます ✓.

かえる means going back home (or to the country or city where you live). Going back to the university after lunch is not かえる: だいがくに かえります ✗, unless you live there. To "go back" to any other place, Japanese uses another verb (もどる), which is not in this lesson.
howToStudy: Say out loud 3 places you always go to and 1 place you don't: 〜に いきます / 〜に いきません.
Read out loud 5 destinations with へ, making sure you say "e": にほんへ, うちへ, がっこうへ, リオへ, だいがくへ.
In your notebook, write 3 pairs with different places: "I go to the library" (としょかんに いきます) × "I study at the library" (としょかんで べんきょうします).

grammar.title: は: topic and contrast
grammar.explanation:
You know は from lesson 01-1: it marks the **TOPIC**, what the sentence is going to talk about ("as for X…"). With verbs, the topic is usually the person: わたしは おちゃを のみます ("as for me, I drink tea").
• は is the sentence's **heading**, not a "who does it" label. Often the topic is the one doing the action (わたしは), but many things can become the topic: the person, the object, the place, the time.
• **Contrast:** は also sets one thing against another, whether the other is said or only implied. コーヒーは のみます。おさけは のみません。 = "Coffee, I drink. Alcohol, I don't." English does something similar when it moves the object to the front and stresses it.
• When the object becomes the topic, **は replaces を**: おさけを → おさけは.
• With で and に, **は comes after** and the particle stays: うちでは ("at home, …"), がっこうには ("to school, …").
• In a negative sentence, は often sounds like contrast: "not this (but something else, yes)".
• If the topic is already clear, it disappears: you don't need to repeat わたしは in every sentence.
grammar.structure: [topic] は …  ·  contrast: A は 〜ます。B は 〜ません。

examples.jp: コーヒーは のみます。おさけは のみません。
examples.kana: コーヒーは のみます。おさけは のみません。
examples.romaji: Kōhī wa nomimasu. Osake wa nomimasen.
examples.en: Coffee, I drink. Alcohol, I don't. [lit. as for coffee, (I) drink; as for alcohol, (I) don't drink]

examples.jp: うちでは べんきょうしません。としょかんで べんきょうします。
examples.kana: うちでは べんきょうしません。としょかんで べんきょうします。
examples.romaji: Uchi de wa benkyō shimasen. Toshokan de benkyō shimasu.
examples.en: At home, I don't study. I study at the library.

examples.jp: たなかさんは テレビを みます。すずきさんは みません。
examples.kana: たなかさんは テレビを みます。すずきさんは みません。
examples.romaji: Tanaka-san wa terebi o mimasu. Suzuki-san wa mimasen.
examples.en: Mr./Ms. Tanaka watches TV. Mr./Ms. Suzuki doesn't.

pitfalls: は and を don't go together: おさけをは のみません ✗ → おさけは のみません ✓.
では is written with は and read "de wa": うちでわ ✗ → うちでは ✓.
The topic is not always the one doing the action. おさけは のみません: "the alcohol doesn't drink" ✗ → "alcohol, (I) don't drink (it)" ✓.
howToStudy: Speaking: make 3 true contrast pairs about yourself (food, drinks, places): 〜は 〜ます。〜は 〜ません。
Tap 🔬 on the coffee example: the blocks with は show up as TOPIC, even though they are things. Compare it with the same sentence using を (コーヒーを のみます), where the block is an OBJECT.
Take 3 sentences with を from the homework and turn the object into a contrast (を → は), adding a second sentence with the opposite.

grammar.title: Word order: putting the blocks together
grammar.gloss: verb at the end; topic and time at the start
grammar.explanation:
Now put it all together. A Japanese sentence is a **row of labeled blocks**, and the **PREDICATE** (the verb in ます) closes the row. The most common order is this:
• 1st **TOPIC** [〜は]: who or what the sentence is about.
• 2nd **TIME** [きょう, あした, こんばん…]: when. These words take no particle; clock times take に (lesson 03-3).
• 3rd **PLACE** [〜で] or **DESTINATION** [〜に / へ]: where it happens, or where someone goes.
• 4th **OBJECT** [〜を]: what.
• 5th **PREDICATE** [〜ます / 〜ません]: what happens. **Always at the end.**
**Two fixed rules:** the predicate stays at the end, and each particle stays **stuck right after** its word.
**One flexible rule:** the blocks in the middle can swap places, because the labels say which is which. わたしは としょかんで ほんを よみます and わたしは ほんを としょかんで よみます mean the same thing (the first is more common). Time and topic can also swap at the start: こんばん、わたしは…
**How to READ:** go straight to the end, find the ★ predicate (よみます, "read") and ask it questions: what? → ほんを. Where? → としょかんで. Who? → わたしは.
**How to BUILD:** after the topic, Japanese is roughly English in a mirror: "(I) read books at the library today" → きょう · としょかんで · ほんを · よみます. So choose the verb and write it at the end of the line; then fill in from right to left: object → place or destination → time → topic.
**Questions:** replace the block with the question word, in the same place, and put か at the end: どこで ほんを よみますか。 / なにを よみますか。
grammar.structure: [topic] は + [time] + [place] で / [destination] に + [object] を + [verb]ます

examples.jp: アナさんは きょう だいがくで にほんごを べんきょうします。
examples.kana: アナさんは きょう だいがくで にほんごを べんきょうします。
examples.romaji: Ana-san wa kyō daigaku de nihongo o benkyō shimasu.
examples.en: Today Ana will study Japanese at the university. [topic · time · place · object · predicate]

examples.jp: ペドロさんは しゅうまつ サンパウロに いきます。
examples.kana: ペドロさんは しゅうまつ サンパウロに いきます。
examples.romaji: Pedoro-san wa shūmatsu Sanpauro ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Pedro is going to São Paulo on the weekend. [topic · time · destination · predicate]

examples.jp: こんばん、わたしは うちで えいがを みます。
examples.kana: こんばん、わたしは うちで えいがを みます。
examples.romaji: Konban, watashi wa uchi de eiga o mimasu.
examples.en: Tonight I'm going to watch a movie at home. [time · topic · place · object · predicate]

pitfalls: The verb doesn't go in the middle, as it does in English: わたしは のみます おちゃを ✗ → わたしは おちゃを のみます ✓.
English prepositions come before the noun ("at home"); Japanese particles always come after it: でうち ✗ → うちで ✓.
Translating in English order gives a broken sentence. "Pedro is going to Rio tomorrow": ペドロさんは いきます リオに あした ✗ → ペドロさんは あした リオに いきます ✓.
Don't forget the labels on the middle blocks: うち おんがく ききます ✗ → うちで おんがくを ききます ✓. In casual conversation some particles drop, but in polite speech — and while you are learning — write all of them.
howToStudy: ヅオリンゴー → Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end: 5 sentences. Always start with the ★ PREDICATE and work to the left.

On paper: write each block of the first example (アナさんは / きょう / だいがくで / にほんごを / べんきょうします) on a small slip, shuffle them and rebuild the sentence out loud. Then swap うちで and えいがを in the third example and notice that the meaning doesn't change.
Reading from the end: take 3 sentences from this lesson (or from Wagotabi), read the verb first and ask the questions out loud: what? where? where to? when? who?

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook, writing the Japanese in kana. In the building tasks, write the verb first, at the end of the line, and fill in toward the left. Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day.

tasks.prompt: Fill in を, で, に / へ or は.

items.q: わたしは まいにち コーヒー＿ のみます。
マリアさんは としょかん＿ べんきょうします。
items.note: She DOES something there: the place of the action.

items.q: ルーカスさんは あした リオ＿ いきます。
コーヒーは のみます。でも、おちゃ＿ のみません。
items.note: Contrast: おちゃ becomes a topic, and は replaces を.

items.q: がっこう＿ ひるごはんを たべます。
items.note: Eating is an activity: the place takes で.

items.q: たなかさんは にほん＿ かえります。
items.note: かえる is movement: a destination with に / へ.

tasks.prompt: Put the blocks in order and write the sentence. Then write the job of each block above it (topic, time, place, destination, object, predicate). Tip: find the verb first (it goes at the end) and the topic (it goes at the start).

items.q: のみます ／ わたしは ／ おちゃを

a.jp: わたしは おちゃを のみます。

items.q: よみます ／ としょかんで ／ アナさんは ／ ざっしを

a.jp: アナさんは としょかんで ざっしを よみます。
a.romaji: Ana-san wa toshokan de zasshi o yomimasu.
a.en: topic · place · object · ★ predicate. "Ana reads magazines at the library."

items.q: かえりません ／ こんばん ／ やまださんは ／ うちに

a.jp: やまださんは こんばん うちに かえりません。
a.romaji: Yamada-san wa konban uchi ni kaerimasen.
a.en: topic · time · destination · ★ predicate. "Mr./Ms. Yamada isn't going home tonight."

items.note: こんばん、やまださんは… is also correct: time and topic can swap at the start.

items.q: みます ／ しゅうまつ ／ うちで ／ わたしは ／ えいがを

a.jp: わたしは しゅうまつ うちで えいがを みます。
a.romaji: Watashi wa shūmatsu uchi de eiga o mimasu.
a.en: topic · time · place · object · ★ predicate. "On weekends I watch movies at home."

items.note: えいがを うちで みます is also correct: the labels keep each block's job.

items.q: たべます ／ だいがくで ／ ひるごはんを ／ ルーカスさんは ／ きょう

a.jp: ルーカスさんは きょう だいがくで ひるごはんを たべます。
a.romaji: Rūkasu-san wa kyō daigaku de hirugohan o tabemasu.
a.en: topic · time · place · object · ★ predicate. "Today Lucas will eat lunch at the university."

items.q: いきますか ／ どこに ／ あした ／ マリアさんは

a.jp: マリアさんは あした どこに いきますか。
a.romaji: Maria-san wa ashita doko ni ikimasu ka.
a.en: topic · time · destination (question) · ★ predicate. "Where is Maria going tomorrow?"

items.note: The question word sits where the answer block will go: どこに = "where to?".

tasks.prompt: Translate into Japanese, building from the end: write the verb first, at the end of the line, and fill in toward the left (object → place or destination → time → topic).

items.q: I listen to music at home.

a.jp: わたしは うちで おんがくを ききます。
a.romaji: Watashi wa uchi de ongaku o kikimasu.

items.q: Ana is going to the university tomorrow.

a.jp: アナさんは あした だいがくに いきます。
a.romaji: Ana-san wa ashita daigaku ni ikimasu.

items.q: Tonight Pedro will study at home.

a.jp: ペドロさんは こんばん うちで べんきょうします。
a.romaji: Pedoro-san wa konban uchi de benkyō shimasu.

items.q: Meat, I eat. But fish, I don't.

a.jp: にくは たべます。でも、さかなは たべません。
a.romaji: Niku wa tabemasu. Demo, sakana wa tabemasen.

items.note: Contrast: both objects become topics with は, and を disappears. でも (but) is optional.

items.q: Where are you going on the weekend? — I'm going to Rio.

a.jp: しゅうまつ どこに いきますか。— リオに いきます。
a.romaji: Shūmatsu doko ni ikimasu ka. — Rio ni ikimasu.

items.q: Mr. Yamada is going back to Japan.

a.jp: やまださんは にほんに かえります。

tasks.prompt: Write 4 sentences about a day of yours with the full order (topic, time, place or destination, object, verb) and 1 contrast pair with は. Then underline each block with one color per job (one for the topic, another for the place…).

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: わたしは きょう だいがくに いきます。だいがくで にほんごを べんきょうします。としょかんで ざっしを よみます。こんばん うちで ばんごはんを たべます。コーヒーは のみます。でも、おさけは のみません。
a.romaji: Watashi wa kyō daigaku ni ikimasu. Daigaku de nihongo o benkyō shimasu. Toshokan de zasshi o yomimasu. Konban uchi de bangohan o tabemasu. Kōhī wa nomimasu. Demo, osake wa nomimasen.
a.en: Today I'm going to the university. At the university, I study Japanese. At the library, I read magazines. Tonight I'll eat dinner at home. Coffee, I drink. But alcohol, I don't.

items.note: Check: the verb is at the end of every sentence; で where you DO something, に where you GO; わたしは only in the first sentence; in the contrast, は in place of を.

workbook.tip: Do it after point 4a; check it with the official Genki Answer Key.
Do it after points 4b and 4c: it is the で × に drill.

practice.what: Play, and at every line ending in 〜ます or 〜ません, pause: find the verb at the end and hunt for the blocks with を, で, に / へ and は. Copy 3 sentences into your notebook and write the job above each block. Then log the session in Immersion → Games and paste one of them into 🔬 Anatomy to check.
Drills → Particles (を, で, に, へ, は). Then 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end: 5 sentences.
Journal: write 3 sentences about your plans for today, each with a place (で) or a destination (に). Use "Anatomy of what I wrote" to see whether each block got the job you wanted.
Tap 🔊 on the examples and repeat them, making a tiny pause after each particle: アナさんは | きょう | だいがくで | にほんごを | べんきょうします. This trains your ear to separate the blocks.
Describe out loud 3 places in your home or your city and what you do in each one (〜で 〜を 〜ます), plus 2 places you go to (〜に いきます). Record yourself and listen: was the verb always at the end?

culture.title: Taking off your shoes: the げんかん and slippers
culture.body: In Japanese homes, right inside the door there is an area called the **げんかん**, usually one step lower than the rest of the floor. That is where you **take off your shoes** before stepping up, and it is customary to leave them pointing toward the door. Many homes offer slippers (スリッパ) to wear inside, but they come off before you step onto たたみ, the woven straw mats. The toilet often has its own pair of slippers just for that room: remember to switch back when you leave. The same goes for some traditional restaurants, temples, schools and clinics, which have shoe racks or small lockers at the entrance.
culture.try: Set up a mini-げんかん at your door: shoes off, pointing toward the street. Every time you come home, say ただいま (lesson 00-3) and one sentence from this lesson about what you are going to do now, with で: うちで ばんごはんを たべます。
